transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I, um, I hope I'm not making a big deal out of nothing, but I guess I'm just having a little trouble keeping my mind on one thing lately. 

I work at a warehouse—doing inventory and moving stock around—and usually I'm a very reliable worker, I really am. But recently, it's like every little noise pulls me away from what I'm doing. If a forklift alarm goes off, or a beeper sounds, or even if someone is just moving a pallet across the floor... my attention just completely snaps over to it. 

And then, well, I'm a bit embarrassed to admit this because I really pride myself on doing good work, but I lose my count. I've actually put the wrong numbers into the inventory system a few times because I got so distracted. I feel just awful about messing up. I just want to get back to doing a good job, you know? Is that... is that the sort of thing you can help me with?
Has this trouble with being easily distracted been a problem for you your whole life, or is it something that's started relatively recently?

Oh, no, no, I've always been very focused. I mean, I've always taken a lot of pride in my work. It's really just been... well, maybe for about a month now? 

It seemed to start right around the time my husband stopped working outside the home. Our whole usual routine just completely changed, and I guess I haven't adjusted very well. I mean, I'm sure it's just a silly adjustment period, right? I hope I'm not wasting your time with something so minor, but it really has only been the last four weeks or so. Does that make sense?
Do you find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless, like you need to get up and move around, especially when you're trying to focus on a task?

Well, I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I'm bouncing off the walls or anything at work. I stay at my station. But, um... it's more like when I get home. 

Usually, after a long shift moving boxes and doing inventory, I'm pretty worn out. But lately... I don't know, I just come home kind of... buzzing? Like, sitting down on the couch to watch TV with my husband just feels almost impossible. So instead, I've been, you know, reorganizing the kitchen cabinets, or going out to the garage to sort through all the storage bins. 

I mean, it's nice to get things clean and organized, right? It's not a bad thing to be productive. I just... I hope it's normal to have a little extra energy sometimes. Is that okay?
Do you find yourself interrupting others or blurting out answers before they finish speaking?

Well, um... I really try to be polite, I promise I do. I don't want to be rude to anyone. But, I guess... my husband and some of the folks at the warehouse have mentioned that I've been talking a little... much? 

They say I just sort of rattle on about all these new recipes I want to try, or ideas I have for making the warehouse safer, or these art classes I've been looking into. And they joke that they can't even get a word in edgewise. I always apologize, of course! It's just... I get so excited about these things, and I feel this, like, pressure in my chest to get it all out. If I don't finish the thought right then, I'm afraid it'll just disappear completely. 

I really don't mean to talk over anyone, though. I'm just enthusiastic, I suppose. That's not too terrible, is it?
Have you been engaging in impulsive behaviors, like spending money excessively or making impulsive decisions, recently?

Well... I wouldn't call it impulsive, exactly. I mean, I've always liked being creative, and it's good to have hobbies, right? 

But, um... I guess maybe I did go a little overboard at a few craft markets recently. I just... I had all these wonderful ideas for projects, and I was so sure I could make some really beautiful things for the house. So I bought, you know, some paints, and a bunch of frames, and a few new tools. It all seemed so useful at the time! 

But... well, I haven't quite gotten around to starting the projects yet. And when the credit card bill came... oh, I was just so embarrassed. I really shouldn't have spent that much, especially with my husband not working right now. I feel terrible about it. But I'm going to return what I can, I promise! Everyone splurges a little sometimes, though, don't they? I'm sure I'll get it under control.
Are you finding it difficult to get along with your husband or coworkers because of these recent changes in your behavior?

Well, um... I really try to get along with everyone. I think it's so important to keep the peace, you know? 

But I guess... maybe things have been just a tiny bit tense lately. At work, I've had to go back and double-check things with my supervisor because I made a few little mistakes on the inventory. I just felt awful about it, taking up his time like that. I'm usually so careful! 

And at home... well, my husband recently retired, and we were so looking forward to spending more time together. But lately, we've been bickering a bit more than usual. Nothing major, I promise! It's just... it feels a little like we're walking on eggshells around each other, instead of just relaxing and enjoying his retirement. 

I'm sure it's just an adjustment period, right? Everyone goes through rough patches when there's a big change like retirement. I'm really trying my best to be patient and understanding. I hope that's the right way to handle it?
Have you had to cut back on any activities or responsibilities because of these distractions and increased energy?

Oh, no, um... I really don't think I've had to cut back on anything. I would absolutely hate to let anyone down, you know? 

I've always prided myself on being a hard worker at the warehouse, and I always make sure my duties are done. Even if I get a little sidetracked with my ideas, I still finish my shifts. If anything, with all this extra energy, I feel like I've been trying to take on a little more! I still get my regular work done, and I keep up with the house... well, mostly, aside from the craft supplies I mentioned earlier. 

I certainly haven't dropped any of my responsibilities. It's just so important to pull your own weight and be dependable, isn't it? I really do try my very best to be reliable for everyone.
Are you feeling overwhelmed or stressed by these changes in your behavior and attention?

Oh, no... I wouldn't use the word overwhelmed. I really try not to let things get to me, you know? 

I mean, I actually like staying active and busy. It keeps me moving, which I think is so important, especially doing physical work at the warehouse at my age. I just try to take everything one day at a time. I guess... well, maybe I was just a tiny bit stressed when I saw that credit card bill for the craft things, but overall? I feel quite fine. I really do. 

I'm managing it all okay. I just think it's always best to keep a positive attitude and keep smiling through things, don't you think? I really hope I'm handling everything the right way.
Do you feel like these changes in your behavior and attention are affecting your overall quality of life?

Oh, goodness, no. I really wouldn't say that at all. I mean... I feel very blessed, honestly. I have a steady job at the warehouse, and even with our little adjustment period lately, my husband and I have a lovely life together. I think it's so important to just focus on the positive and count your blessings, you know? 

So, no, I don't think it's hurting my quality of life or anything like that. I'm just... well, maybe just a little more energetic and a tiny bit scattered right now, but I'm still doing all the things I need to do. I really do try my hardest to be a good wife and a good worker. I'm doing okay, aren't I? I just hope I'm not making a fuss over nothing.
Do you feel like these changes in your behavior are causing you a lot of distress or worry?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I really try not to be a worrier. I mean, there's no sense in getting all worked up over every little thing, right? 

I just... I like to think I'm taking it all in stride. Like I said, maybe that one bill was a little bit of a shock, but I'm certainly not losing sleep or feeling distressed about it. I just want to keep being helpful and doing my part. I really hope I'm not giving you the impression that I'm falling apart or anything, because I'm honestly doing just fine. I think I'm handling it all reasonably well, don't you?
Are you having trouble meeting your responsibilities at work or at home because of your recent behavior and attention changes?

Well, I wouldn't use the word *trouble*, exactly. I always try to give a hundred percent, wherever I am. I mean... I suppose I did have a tiny little mix-up with some inventory at the warehouse recently. I've just had to double-check a few things with my supervisor, just to make absolutely sure everything is correct. I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job for them, you know? 

And at home... well, it's just a bit of an adjustment phase right now. My husband recently retired, which is such a blessing, but... I admit we have been having a few more little disagreements than usual. I guess it feels a bit like we’re walking around each other right now, instead of just settling into his retirement peacefully like we planned. 

But I'm still getting the house taken care of and working all my shifts! It’s perfectly normal for couples to have a little friction when routines change, don't you think? I really am trying my very best to keep everything running smoothly. I hope I'm still doing okay.
Are you having any difficulty getting along with your coworkers or supervisor at the warehouse due to your recent behavior changes?

Oh, goodness, no. Everybody at the warehouse is just lovely, really. I mean, they're like a second family to me. I haven't had any trouble getting along with anyone. 

I suppose... well, sometimes I can get a little chatty when I'm feeling this energetic, and maybe I talk a tiny bit faster than usual, but nobody seems to mind. I think they just see it as me being enthusiastic about the work. I always try to be a team player and keep everyone's spirits up. I certainly wouldn't want to be a bother to anyone, especially my supervisor. I'm still doing a good job being friendly and cooperative, right? I just want to make sure I'm being a good coworker.
Are there any activities or tasks that you used to enjoy or find easy, but now find difficult due to your recent behavior and attention changes?

Oh, no, I don't think so. Honestly... if anything, I feel like I have even more energy for the things I enjoy right now. 

I'm still doing my gardening on the weekends, and, um, keeping up with my reading and all my little projects around the house. I haven't found anything to be difficult at all, really. I always try to stay active and keep up with my interests. I think it's so important to stay engaged with the things you love, don't you? 

I promise I'm still doing all the things I'm supposed to be doing. I hope that's the kind of thing you were asking about? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm letting myself go or giving up on my hobbies, because I'm definitely not.
Have you noticed any problems in your relationships with friends or family members due to your recent behavior changes?

Oh, goodness, no. My friends and family mean the absolute world to me. I mean... well, like I mentioned earlier, my husband and I are just figuring out his new retirement schedule, but that's just normal everyday stuff, right? You don't think that counts as a *problem*, do you? 

As for my friends, everything is just wonderful. I always make sure to keep in touch and... and remember everyone's birthdays. If anything, I think they actually enjoy it when I'm a little more upbeat and energetic! I would just absolutely hate to think I was ever being a burden or rubbing anyone the wrong way. I really do try my hardest to be a good friend and a good wife. I hope I'm still doing okay in that department.
Do you think your recent behavior changes have significantly impacted your ability to function at work or in your daily life?

Well, um... "significantly" is a strong word, isn't it? I wouldn't say significantly. I'm still showing up every day and doing my very best. 

I suppose... well, I did have to double-check with my supervisor a couple of times recently because of some silly little inventory errors I made. Just rushing a bit too much, I think. But I caught them, and I'm being extra careful now. That shows I'm being responsible, right? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job for them. 

And at home... well, I mentioned my husband's retirement. We've just had a few more disagreements than usual lately. It's nothing terrible, just... it feels a little bit like we're walking on eggshells around each other right now, instead of just relaxing into this new phase of our lives. But that's just an adjustment period, don't you think? Every couple goes through that. I'm sure it's not a big deal, right? I really am trying my hardest to make things smooth at work and at home.
Are you feeling distressed about the changes in your behavior and attention?

Oh, distressed? No, no, I wouldn't say I'm distressed. I mean, I feel pretty good, honestly. 

I know I mentioned the little mix-ups at work and the bickering with my husband, but... well, I don't want you to think I'm falling apart or anything like that. I'm really trying to keep a positive attitude about everything. I think staying positive is half the battle, don't you? 

I just... I want to make sure I'm handling everything the way I should be. I'm not doing anything terribly wrong, am I? I'm just trying to keep up with it all and be helpful. I promise I'm not letting things get out of hand.
Are you finding it difficult to maintain your relationships or meet your responsibilities due to these recent changes in your behavior?

Oh, difficult? No, no, I wouldn't use that word at all. I mean, I'm keeping up with everything just fine, really. 

Like I said, I'm still going to work every day and doing my absolute best moving the freight and keeping track of the stock. I haven't missed a single shift! And with my husband... well, we're just adjusting, like any couple would. It's not difficult, just... a little transition phase. 

I really am meeting all my responsibilities, I promise. I would feel just awful if I was letting anyone down or dropping the ball. You don't think I'm failing at any of this, do you? I'm really trying my hardest to make sure everyone is happy and everything gets done.
Are you feeling like you're unable to fulfill your roles at work or at home because of these changes in your behavior?

Oh, unable? No, I definitely wouldn't say unable. I know we sort of just touched on this, and I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, but I really am keeping up with things. 

Like I mentioned before, I've just had to double-check with my supervisor a few times lately because I made those silly little inventory errors with the stock. But I'm fixing them! I just want to make sure I get the freight moved exactly right so they don't think poorly of me. Seeking a little extra help to get it right means I'm still doing a good job, doesn't it? 

And at home... well, I know I brought up the arguments with my husband. We've just been bickering enough lately that it kind of feels like we're just walking around each other, instead of really settling into his retirement and enjoying the time together. But I'm still taking care of things around the house and trying to be a good wife. I'm not failing at my roles, am I? I really hope you don't think I'm someone who can't handle her own life. I'm truly doing my very best to keep everyone happy.
Have you experienced any significant feelings of guilt or self-criticism related to your recent behavior changes?

Guilt? Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say guilt. I mean, nobody's perfect, right? 

I know I've been a little... well, maybe a little distracted with the inventory slip-ups, and the bickering at home isn't ideal. But I don't sit around beating myself up over it or anything. I just try to look at what happened, figure out how to do it better the next day, and keep moving forward. That's the healthy way to handle it, isn't it? 

I really try not to be too hard on myself, because I know I'm putting in a lot of effort. I'm just trying to be a good employee and a good wife. I hope I'm coming across that way... I'm not doing too badly, am I?
Have you felt like your recent behavior changes have caused significant problems in your relationships or work performance?

Oh, um, significant problems? No, I wouldn't call them significant problems. I know we keep sort of circling back to this, and I hope I'm explaining it okay... 

Like I mentioned, I just had to double-check things with my supervisor a bit because of those silly little inventory errors. But that just means I'm being thorough, right? Making sure the freight is exactly where it needs to be. And at home, yes, my husband and I have been arguing a bit, and we're kind of walking around each other right now instead of just enjoying his retirement like we planned... but that's normal for couples going through a transition, isn't it? 

I really don't think these are huge, significant problems. I'm still trying my very best at everything. I'm doing okay, don't you think?
